title: Deliver a clean packaged pkl-parser proof through direct Spoon translation
description:
## Outcome

Deliver the first architectural proof required by vibeformer/doc/architecture.md: translate the complete upstream pkl-parser production module directly from a resolved Spoon semantic model into disposable C#, compile it from scratch, pack it, consume it independently, and compare observable behavior with upstream Pkl.

## Current evidence and history

- Vibeformer is intentionally reset to deps.edn and durable docs; no src, test, generator, or package project currently exists.
- The removed implementation grew through 179 sample-, inferred-fact-, no-classpath-, and Datomic-oriented beads and roughly 29K lines before the direct-translation reset. Do not recreate that path.
- The prior cleared epic pkl-ygbtd stated the full parser goal but had no executable child graph.
- The pinned research/pkl gitlink is f7cac257ade5775c1dfc255f4fda2eacc296e9d0.
- pkl-parser has 50 production Java files plus org/pkl/parser/errorMessages.properties, totaling 9,023 production lines. Its main compile classpath is JSpecify 1.0.0. Five upstream Kotlin test files and the LanguageSnippetTests corpus provide independent behavior evidence.

## Architectural constraints

- Use Spoon with the real production source set, resources, generated inputs if any, and resolved Gradle compile classpath. Accepted generation must not use no-classpath mode.
- Walk live Spoon frontend objects directly and recursively. Do not serialize or reconstruct a second AST, add a database, or reparse Java source text.
- Select type, executable, constructor, and field mappings from resolved symbol identity, including overload and generic information.
- Account for every reachable production declaration and executable body. Unsupported or unresolved semantics are blocking diagnostics; never silently skip, stub, or name-guess.
- Generated C# is disposable and receives no manual patches. Fix resolution, recursive translation, symbol mappings, project emission, or an explicitly owned focused helper, then regenerate.
- Use ordinary .NET APIs where they preserve behavior. Keep Pkl parser behavior in the generated/product implementation, not a generic compatibility runtime.
- Kotlin remains governed by the full product goal; when production Kotlin translation is reached it must use PSI plus the Kotlin Analysis API. This Java architectural proof is not an exclusion or a claim of project completion.

## Success Criteria

- A clean checkout at the pinned gitlink has one reproducible path that regenerates all pkl-parser C# and project/package inputs without manual edits.
- The resolved-model and recursive-coverage gates report zero unresolved, ambiguous, fallback, skipped, unsupported, or public-stub items for all production inputs.
- Fresh generated output builds and packs with compiler diagnostics mapped back to Spoon elements and translation/mapping rules.
- An independent .NET consumer, outside the generated solution, restores the produced NuGet package and exercises public lexer, parser, span, syntax-model, and error surfaces.
- A separately run upstream JVM oracle and the independent package consumer agree on representative upstream valid and invalid corpus behavior, including tokens, syntax structure, spans, and diagnostics where observable.
- Exact clean-generation, test, build, pack, consume, and differential commands and results are recorded on the beads that close them.
- Closing this epic proves only the first architectural module milestone; vibeformer/doc/product-goal.md remains the exclusive project-completion rule.

title: Bootstrap the reproducible Vibeformer execution and test harness
description:
## Outcome

Create the minimal Clojure execution and test spine that later children can use from a clean checkout, without restoring the deleted fact database, old emitter, sample runner, or copied sample-project architecture.

## Implementation requirements

- Provide a stable command/API for clean generation and focused/full tests.
- Treat vibeformer/target as disposable output.
- Locate research/pkl through the tracked submodule, verify the expected gitlink revision, and fail clearly when the submodule or required toolchain is unavailable.
- Derive the complete pkl-parser production source/resource inputs from the actual Gradle project rather than a handwritten file allowlist.
- Preserve the research submodule as read-only.
- Establish focused tests for command failure, clean output setup, source/resource discovery, and deterministic configuration.

## Acceptance criteria

- Starting without vibeformer/target, the harness starts successfully with the tracked pkl-parser module and reports all 50 current production Java files plus errorMessages.properties.
- A mismatched/missing submodule, missing classpath input, or toolchain failure is explicit and nonzero.
- Tests can run from vibeformer using committed aliases/tasks and do not depend on developer-local absolute paths.
- No database, normalized/reconstructed AST, copied upstream source tree, generated C# patch, or source-text parser is introduced.
- Exact test and clean-start commands/results are recorded when closing this bead.
notes:

title: Build a fail-closed resolved Spoon model for complete pkl-parser
description:
## Outcome

Load the complete pkl-parser production module into Spoon with its real Gradle source set and compile classpath, retaining live Spoon objects for direct translation.

## Implementation requirements

- Configure Spoon with no-classpath disabled and Java language settings derived from the upstream project.
- Include all production Java inputs and any generated production inputs discovered by the project model; include JSpecify 1.0.0 from the actual compile classpath.
- Traverse type uses, executable/constructor references, field references, inheritance, generic bounds/arguments, annotations, and source positions to enforce semantic resolution.
- Distinguish project-local declarations from JDK/dependency symbols using resolved declarations and stable symbol keys.
- Do not turn missing resolution into inferred package roots, simple-name guesses, or source-text heuristics.
- Pass live CtElement/CtReference objects to later stages; no serialized fact model or database is allowed.

## Acceptance criteria

- The model includes every production compilation unit at the pinned gitlink and excludes test/build-only sources from product translation.
- Resolution tests exercise project-local nested/generic symbols, overloads, constructors, fields, JSpecify annotations, and representative JDK APIs actually used by pkl-parser.
- Accepted model construction has zero shadow, unresolved, ambiguous, or fallback symbols; failures include source location and frontend identity.
- Re-running model construction is deterministic and does not modify research/pkl.
- Exact focused/full test commands and resolution totals are recorded when closing this bead.
close_reason: Completed fail-closed live Spoon model for the pinned complete pkl-parser Gradle main source set. Discovery: Java release 17, preview false, 50 production compilation units, one resource, JSpecify 1.0.0 compile classpath; tests exclude test/build-only sources and verify research/pkl tracked status is unchanged across deterministic reruns. Resolution totals: 114 project types, 36,174 type uses, 2,600 executable references, 855 constructor references, 2,555 field references, 372 annotations, 1,145 stable symbols; shadow-only=0, unresolved=0, ambiguous=0, fallback=0. Focused: cd vibeformer && clojure -M:test --namespace vibeformer.spoon-test (4 tests, 30 assertions). Full: cd vibeformer && clojure -M:test (12 tests, 55 assertions). Generation: cd vibeformer && clojure -M:run generate (clean complete model with identical totals).

title: Implement the direct recursive Java translation kernel and coverage gate
description:
## Outcome

Implement the reusable fail-closed recursion from live Spoon elements to structured C# translation results before adding pkl-parser-specific breadth.

## Implementation requirements

- Dispatch structurally on Spoon node kinds and recurse through live children for declarations, types, statements, and expressions.
- Carry destination node/text, source element identity/location, rule identity, resolved-symbol mapping identity, required usings/helpers, diagnostics, and source mappings in each result.
- Define semantic mapping registries keyed by resolved type, executable/constructor, and field identity rather than simple names or printed source.
- Enforce precedence/nesting and deterministic child-result combination in a small structured C# writer.
- Produce a blocking diagnostic for every unsupported reachable element/reference. Diagnostic/fallback mode must never satisfy accepted generation.
- Build coverage from actual recursive visits, not a separately reconstructed inventory.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests use live elements from the complete resolved pkl-parser model and demonstrate recursive parent/child translation, resolved mapping dispatch, deterministic output, source mappings, and aggregated diagnostics.
- Removing a rule or mapping makes the coverage gate fail at the originating Spoon element with an actionable identity and location.
- No source-text reparsing, second AST, database, silent skip, placeholder implementation, or broad reflection/name fallback exists.
- The kernel remains reusable for later Java projects and contains no embedded Pkl parser implementation.
- Exact focused/full test commands and covered/blocked node totals are recorded when closing this bead.
close_reason: Completed the reusable fail-closed direct Spoon recursion kernel and structured C# writer. The live complete-resolved-model Span.stopIndexExclusive gate records 28 actual recursive visits: 16 structural and 12 resolved-semantic; covered=28, blocked=0, unsupported=0, missing mappings=0, missing occurrences=0, fallback=0. Removing the binary rule blocks exactly the originating CtBinaryOperator with source identity/location; removing the resolved Span.length field mapping blocks exactly that field reference; combined independent failures aggregate without parent cascades; diagnostic fallback remains ineligible for accepted generation. Focused kernel: cd vibeformer && clojure -M:test --namespace vibeformer.java-translate-test (5 tests, 33 assertions). Focused writer: cd vibeformer && clojure -M:test --namespace vibeformer.csharp-test (2 tests, 6 assertions). Full: cd vibeformer && clojure -M:test (19 tests, 94 assertions). Clean smoke: cd vibeformer && clojure -M:run generate (50 units, 114 project types, 36,174 type uses, 2,600 calls, 855 constructors, 2,555 fields, 372 annotations, 1,145 symbols; zero shadow/unresolved/ambiguous/fallback). research/pkl tracked status remained unchanged.

title: Emit the complete pkl-parser declaration and project topology
description:
## Outcome

Use the direct recursive kernel to emit the entire pkl-parser type/declaration graph and a disposable C# project/package skeleton, while leaving every not-yet-supported executable construct as a hard failure for the next child.

## Implementation requirements

- Emit namespaces and deterministic files for all production classes, interfaces, enums, records, sealed/nested types, fields, constructors, methods, parameters, generic constraints, visibility, modifiers, and annotations with runtime relevance.
- Preserve project-local type relationships and public API shape through resolved symbol mappings.
- Derive target framework, nullable settings, project/package metadata, resources, and output paths from explicit destination configuration.
- Carry errorMessages.properties through a deliberate resource/mapping strategy without hand-copying data into generated code.
- Generate only from live Spoon objects; do not use printed Java or a mirrored declaration AST.
- Do not emit empty/default/throwing bodies as accepted output. Remaining body work must stay in blocking diagnostics owned by the next child.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 50 production Java compilation units and the resource are deterministically accounted for in generated project inputs or explicit hard failures.
- Every source declaration has a source mapping and every generated declaration traces to a Spoon element/rule.
- Full-model declaration coverage is zero-skip and duplicate/collision checks are clean.
- Two clean generations are byte-for-byte stable.
- No generated file is manually edited and no executable stub is treated as implemented.
- Exact generation/test commands, declaration totals, and remaining hard-failure totals are recorded when closing this bead.
close_reason: Completed direct live-Spoon declaration and project emission. Configuration: vibeformer/config/pkl-parser.edn drives net8.0, nullable, assembly/package metadata, namespaces, output paths, and embedded errorMessages.properties handling; the resource is copied byte-for-byte, never hand-embedded. Clean generation: cd vibeformer && clojure -M:run generate. Result: 50/50 compilation units accounted, 47 deterministic C# files, 114 types, 1 resource, 1,947 declarations (114 types, 79 fields, 274 enum values, 97 constructors, 675 methods, 603 parameters, 26 record components, 79 type parameters), 5,118 source mappings, missing mappings=0, skipped units=0, collisions=0. All 372 annotations have resolved decisions (192 Override, 42 SuppressWarnings, 135 Nullable, 3 NullMarked); nullable metadata/context is carried deliberately. Focused: cd vibeformer && clojure -M:test --namespace vibeformer.java-project-test (1 test, 19 assertions). Full: cd vibeformer && clojure -M:test (20 tests, 114 assertions). Two clean generations were byte-for-byte stable with identical aggregate SHA-256 fd4f6fb768e392a4ad8d55354351b562c21d9f42cba076e4fd55b75fda476905. Fail-closed compiler check: cd vibeformer && dotnet build target/generated/pkl-parser/Pkl.Parser.csproj --nologo --verbosity:minimal -p:RestoreIgnoreFailedSources=true restored successfully and reported exactly 983 deliberate CS1029 blockers, 0 warnings: 691 executable bodies, 18 field initializers, 274 enum-value initializers. No empty/default/throwing implementation is accepted; pkl-fzc.5 owns those executable blockers. research/pkl tracked status remained unchanged.

title: Close pkl-parser executable-body and resolved-symbol mapping coverage
description:
## Outcome

Translate every reachable pkl-parser production method, constructor, and initializer body directly from Spoon and reduce the accepted-generation coverage gate to zero blockers.

## Implementation requirements

- Add structural translation for the statements/expressions actually present across the complete module, including modern switch forms, loops, pattern matching, lambdas/method references, nested construction, exceptions, and initialization semantics.
- Translate project-local calls/fields/constructors through resolved declarations.
- Add explicit resolved mappings for the JDK surfaces actually used, including strings/Unicode Character behavior, arrays, collections/deques/lists, streams/collectors, Objects, Supplier, ResourceBundle, Locale, and MessageFormat.
- Preserve Java evaluation order, equality/hash behavior, mutability, iterator order, numeric/character behavior, and exception semantics where observable.
- Prefer ordinary .NET APIs. Any helper request must identify the semantic gap and ownership boundary and be ordinary reviewable C# source.
- Drive work from full-module hard failures, not newly invented sample projects; add focused regressions from real failing Spoon nodes as needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- Accepted generation over all production inputs reports zero unsupported/unresolved/ambiguous/fallback/skipped nodes or symbol mappings.
- Generated public and internal executable bodies contain no NotImplementedException, default-return, empty-body, TODO, or equivalent implementation placeholders.
- Focused tests cover each semantic mapping family and regression tests point to the upstream construct that required it.
- Source mappings connect all generated executable constructs to Spoon elements and translation/mapping rules.
- Exact focused/full test and generation commands plus final coverage totals are recorded when closing this bead.

Generation: cd vibeformer && rm -rf target/generated/pkl-parser && clojure -M:run generate; 50/50 units, 48 C# files including one reviewable Java compatibility source, 1 resource, 1,947 declarations, 31,611 emitted source mappings, hard failures=0, skips=0, collisions=0. Two clean generations had identical aggregate SHA-256 cd0a0a105f429fe618860042ebf783c62df1fcd7d8d41be25f23e067868044ce; placeholder scan found none. Focused: cd vibeformer && clojure -M:test --namespace vibeformer.java-project-test (1 test, 35 assertions). Full: cd vibeformer && clojure -M:test (20 tests, 130 assertions). Both passed. title: Drive generated pkl-parser to deterministic clean compilation
description:
## Outcome

Make freshly generated complete pkl-parser C# compile as an ordinary .NET project with no manual output edits or hidden diagnostic suppression.

## Implementation requirements

- Run dotnet build only on output regenerated from scratch in the same verification path.
- Parse compiler diagnostics and map them back through committed source mappings to Spoon elements and structural/symbol rules.
- Fix failures in frontend configuration, recursive translation, resolved mappings, project emission, or narrowly justified helpers, then regenerate.
- Preserve public API shape and semantics; do not solve compiler errors by dropping reachable declarations, weakening types, renaming around collisions without deterministic mappings, or adding stubs.
- Require deterministic clean regeneration before the accepted build.

## Acceptance criteria

- Removing all disposable generated output and rerunning generation produces byte-stable project inputs that build with zero compiler errors and no ignored/suppressed translator diagnostics.
- Compiler warnings are either eliminated or explicitly demonstrated non-semantic and recorded; no warning may conceal a stub, unreachable omission, nullability contract loss, or unresolved mapping.
- A committed regression maps representative historical compiler failures to source Spoon elements/rules.
- A scan of generated/public code finds zero implementation placeholders.
- Exact clean, generate, test, and dotnet build commands/results are recorded when closing this bead.

title: Pack pkl-parser and prove independent NuGet consumption
description:
## Outcome

Produce a versioned local NuGet package from freshly generated pkl-parser and consume it from an independently created .NET project outside the generated solution.

## Implementation requirements

- Pack only after the clean generation and build gates pass.
- Include the intended public parser API, required runtime/resource assets, package metadata, and no translator/test-only implementation internals.
- Restore the package through a local feed into an independent consumer that has no project reference or source access to generated output.
- Exercise public Lexer, Parser/GenericParser, Span, syntax-model, visitor, and error-message/resource paths through normal package references.
- Make the consume test recreate its project/feed state so success cannot come from stale binaries or a developer NuGet cache.

## Acceptance criteria

- A clean generation produces a NuGet artifact, and an independent consumer restores, builds, and runs against that artifact only.
- The consumer covers representative successful parsing, tokenization, syntax traversal, spans, and parse errors/resource messages.
- Package inspection shows required assemblies/resources and no manual generated-source patches or public stubs.
- The commands are reproducible on the repository toolchain and failures are nonzero.
- Exact clean/pack/restore/build/run commands and artifact identity are recorded when closing this bead.

title: Differentially validate packaged pkl-parser against upstream behavior
description:
## Outcome

Establish independent upstream behavior evidence for the packaged generated parser, beyond translator tests and compilation.

## Implementation requirements

- Run an upstream JVM oracle separately at the pinned research/pkl revision and the independent .NET package consumer from the prior child.
- Compare normalized observable results rather than implementation details: lexer token sequences, parsed syntax structure, source spans/full spans, visitor-visible ordering, and parse error type/message/span where stable.
- Reuse authoritative upstream tests and fixtures, including the LanguageSnippetTests input corpus and LexerTest/SpanTest edge cases, adapting only the harness needed to call each public implementation.
- Include representative valid and invalid Pkl, Unicode identifiers/code points, string interpolation/escapes and CR/LF variants, declarations/types/expressions/object bodies, and diagnostics.
- The translator or generated implementation must not generate its own expected outputs, and the two sides must not share parser implementation code.
- Mismatches are product blockers under this epic; fix durable translator/runtime ownership and rerun rather than adding exclusions.

## Acceptance criteria

- Differential execution runs through the packed package and a separately executed upstream JVM artifact/oracle.
- The selected upstream corpus is enumerated with a reason for any test-harness-only adaptation; no in-scope behavior mismatch is waived.
- All compared cases pass, including observable spans and diagnostics where supported by the public APIs.
- A deliberate perturbation on either side proves the comparison detects a mismatch.
- Exact upstream build/oracle, package-consumer, and differential commands/results and case counts are recorded.
- The epic is closed only after this evidence and all siblings are complete; closure is pkl-parser milestone evidence, not PROJECT_COMPLETED.

title: Review completed work for epic pkl-fzc
description: After epic pkl-fzc (Deliver a clean packaged pkl-parser proof through direct Spoon translation) is complete, review the work done for that epic. Inspect the closed Beads, durable semantic-frontend, recursive-translation, resolved-symbol-mapping, and destination-runtime changes, together with compiler diagnostics, package-consumer results, independent behavior evidence, and any remaining runtime issues. Create follow-up Beads for bugs, cleanup, missing tests, or product-scope gaps that should be fixed. Do not treat generated reports, successful compilation, or completion of the epic as evidence that the overall product goal is complete.
